title: Prefix stencils: First qualifying slip
topics: Two pointers, windows and prefix sums
summary: For each index i, produce the sum from max(0,i-k+1) through i inclusive. These are trailing ranges that may be shorter than k near the left edge. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.
descriptionMd:
A running account lets the stationery desk recover trailing totals without rereading the full tape. Pia needs the first qualifying slip while the courier waits at the door. Later matches must not jump ahead in the tray.

For each index i, produce the sum from max(0,i-k+1) through i inclusive. These are trailing ranges that may be shorter than k near the left edge.

Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.

Implement prefixStencilsFirstQualifyingSlip(readings, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: Prefix range subtraction. For each index i, produce the sum from max(0,i-k+1) through i inclusive. These are trailing ranges that may be shorter than k near the left edge. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with prefix range subtraction. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For each index i, produce the sum from max(0,i-k+1) through i inclusive. These are trailing ranges that may be shorter than k near the left edge. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.
